words: Craig argues philosophers abandoned strict incompatibility because atheists must exclude morally sufficient reasons, but must still show why suffering does not make Christianity improbable.
critique: Strongest feature: Craig challenges logical incompatibility because philosophers abandoned it since atheists must rule out all-morally sufficient divine reasons for evil, making the reply responsive and coherent. Principal limitation: That possibility defense supplies neither evidence of actual sufficient reasons nor a bridge from bare compatibility to the comparative likelihood of Christianity given the scale and distribution of suffering. Live burden: Craig must explain why extensive world-suffering fits Christianity tolerably well, rather than showing that God and some evil could coexist. Locked score: The exact score of 72 fits a substantively-incomplete reply, with responsiveness and relevance stronger because it directly contacts the evil challenge, while evidence warrant and calibration are weaker because possibility is made to bear more probabilistic weight than the supplied support earns.
